content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — 5xx rate > 12% on canary group 'eu-canary-2' since 10:43 UTC. Tripped deploy-health-check.

alice: noticed the canary rolled at 10:41. errors are HTTP 500 from /v1/generate and 'missing column' in app logs.

ben: i'm on it — rolling deploy id 2026-03-15-rls-1987. quick check: we included the migration that adds `session_state` (non-null) but the app change expects the column. canary app started hitting DB inserts that fail.

carol: copying logs from canary pod: ``ERROR: null value in column \"session_state\" violates not-null constraint`` followed by stacktrace.

oncall-db: @ben can you confirm the migration was a forward-only AND ran as part of canary? I see the migration job kicked at 10:40 and finished with success status according to CI, but app errors started at 10:41.

ben: CI reported migration success because the ALTER TABLE ran, but it used `SET NOT NULL` after creating the column without a default. if data paths insert before code populates the field we get failures. i think our canary services started hitting a codepath that inserts rows before the app sets the new field.

tilly: oh no — that means the code change is incompatible with the migration ordering. can we flip a kill-switch for the feature so code avoids the new insert?

ben: attempted to toggle feature flag `session-init-v2` via console at 10:46 but it returned 404 — looks like the flag key in this release is `session_init_v2` (underscore vs dash). human error. trying both keys now.

deploy-bot: feature-flag-change request accepted (key=session_init_v2). propagation to canary in progress.

alice: still seeing 500s, looks like propagation hasn't reached all canary pods. some pods restarted and now fail during boot on migration-backed inserts.

oncall-db: immediate mitigation options: (A) add a temporary nullable column and backfill then set NOT NULL + default in a safe window; (B) alter table to add column WITH DEFAULT and NOT NULL in a single statement (dangerous on huge tables); (C) rollback code release. which is fastest?

ben: rollback is safest from app correctness POV but may not be instantaneous because we already ran the migration on canary DBs. canary DBs are separate replica sets for this rollout, but traffic is leaking from canary to prod in some routing edge cases — early customers in EU are seeing 500s.

cust-suc: 4 customers reported errors (two on EU region) — they see transaction failures in the app. CS is pausing onboarding flows and posting a status update.

oncall-db: ok prioritize minimal blast radius fix: add column nullable and return quickly. run:

```
ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN session_state TEXT;
-- backfill known hotspots with empty JSON
UPDATE sessions SET session_state = '{}' WHERE session_state IS NULL LIMIT 100000;
```

oncall-db: then we can coordinate a fast small migration to SET NOT NULL with default during low traffic if backfill completes.

ben: performing ALTER TABLE on canary DB now (eu-canary-2). running in psql -c.

deploy-bot: db-job eu-canary-2/alter-session_state started by ben at 10:55 UTC.

alice: monitoring error rate — decreasing from 12% -> 3% in last 4 minutes. some pods still 500ing but count shrinking.

oncall-db: backfill chunking script launched (pg-batch-runner) to update 200k rows across shards. ETA ~ 8m.

carol: while that runs, should we revert the release in the control plane? I can trigger canary rollback but want to avoid flipping network routes mid-backfill.

ben: agree. hold rollback until nullable column added and backfill finished. then flip flag or rollback safely.

incident-bot: on-call handover reminder in 30m. next oncall is tilly.

tilly: I'm taking primary once ben drops off. summary for handoff: attempted flag kill failed due to key mismatch; migration added NOT NULL before app change; mitigation = ADD COLUMN nullable + backfill; monitor 500s and customer impact.

cust-suc: public status: "Partial errors in EU during canary deploy; mitigation in progress. Affected customers: internal IDs C-1021, C-1199, C-1205, C-1212. We have paused new signups in EU. Will update in 30m."

alice: backfill completed on eu-canary-2. executing ``ALTER TABLE sessions ALTER COLUMN session_state SET NOT NULL`` with DEFAULT '{}' will be done during quiet window in 5m.

oncall-db: note: SET NOT NULL without rewrite can fail on some engines; using two-step we already added values. proceed.

ben: performing the final SET NOT NULL now.

deploy-bot: db-job eu-canary-2/set-not-null completed at 11:07 UTC.

alice: error rate back to <0.5%. canary health is green.

ben: because the canary DB changed we will still rollback the code to be safe and re-deploy with a properly sequenced migration (create nullable + deploy, backfill, set not null). initiating rollback now.

deploy-bot: rollback started for release 2026-03-15-rls-1987 at 11:10 UTC.

tilly: i'm taking the remainder of the incident. things to document for postmortem: 1) migration order mismatch 2) feature flag key naming led to delayed kill-switch 3) routing leak caused canary traffic to hit a small set of prod users 4) runbook steps that worked (nullable add + fast backfill) 5) consider adding pre-deploy checks for NOT NULL migrations.

cust-suc: updating impacted customers: now telling them errors resolved, rollback in progress, will reach out directly for any residual failures.

carol: rolling notes into incident timeline. handing off to tilly in 25m.

tilly: acknowledged — i'll watch deploy rollback and confirm prod routing normal. next steps: schedule postmortem with DB and release owners, recommend adding automated lint to block NOT NULL migrations without backfill scripts.

incident-bot: incident annotated: severity=sev2, duration=00:33:00, primary-cause=migration-order-incompat, mitigation=nullable-add+backfill+rollback.

tilly: taking over on-call now. closing thread for active paging; will reopen if we see >1% errors in next 15m.
